calls.head: Expect Tampa Bay to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Tampa Bay ranks 6th of 32 for shot volume (60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5); Philadelphia ranks 28th for shot suppression.
calls.call: Tampa Bay takes at least its usual 60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Tampa Bay took 77.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 60.3.

calls.head: Tampa Bay shoots from the point; Philadelphia works down low
calls.body: Tampa Bay ranks 10th of 32 for point-shot reliance, toward the point-heavy end; Philadelphia ranks 27th, toward the down low end.
calls.call: Tampa Bay takes a bigger share of its shots from the point than Philadelphia.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts from the point, Tampa Bay had 36% and Philadelphia 31%. Coming in, Tampa Bay was at 42% and Philadelphia at 39%.

TBL.head: We had this close to even (57% for Tampa Bay), and Tampa Bay came through.

PHI.head: We had this close to even (43% for Philadelphia), and it went Tampa Bay’s way.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 67, against its usual 105 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 10 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia tried a different line
surprises.body: D. Barkey, O. Tippett, T. Zegras played 7:38 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Philadelphia’s usual lines.
